definitions.explanation: Behavior that appears unnatural, nervous, or suspicious. Used both in serious contexts (police reports, security) and casually to describe someone who looks nervous or guilty.

examples.japanese: {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な{人物|じんぶつ}を{見|み}かけた。
examples.english: I spotted a person acting suspiciously.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{質問|しつもん}されると{挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}になった。
examples.english: He started acting suspiciously when questioned.

examples.japanese: {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な{男|おとこ}が{店|みせ}の{前|まえ}をうろうろしていたので、{警察|けいさつ}に{通報|つうほう}した。
examples.english: A man was acting suspiciously, loitering in front of the store, so I called the police.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in police and security contexts for describing suspicious persons, but also used casually and humorously. The shortened slang form {挙動|きょどう}る (kyodoru) means "to act nervously/suspiciously" in informal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}な{人物|じんぶつ} (suspicious person)
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}になる (to start acting suspiciously)
- {挙動|きょどう}{不審|ふしん}で{職務質問|しょくむしつもん}される (to be stopped and questioned for suspicious behavior)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不審者|ふしんしゃ}: suspicious person — focuses on the person rather than the behavior
- {怪|あや}しい: suspicious, fishy — a broader, more casual adjective
